title: Define ephemeral burst handling policy and customer-facing billing clarity for surge boosts
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary:
Customers using Dedicated capacity with burst-enabled fleets observe opaque overage invoices and unpredictable latency when temporary boosts consume surge pools. This ticket defines an ephemeral burst handling policy (how the serving runtime and allocator admit and evict burst traffic), and the customer-facing billing clarity rules (how we charge for temporary boosts and when we apply overage rates).

Background and problem statement:
- Currently we support 'surge pool' and manual/automatic temporary boosts. When bursts occur, requests can be routed to surge capacity without clear guarantees. Billing for those surges shows up as overage line items without clear attribution.
- Key customer complaints: unpredictable cost spikes, inability to distinguish guaranteed throughput vs best-effort burst usage, and lack of console controls to limit burst spend.

Goals:
1) Define a deterministic ephemeral burst policy that the runtime can enforce (admit -> warm-up -> sustain -> evict).
2) Add API + Console controls to cap burst spend and opt into 'graceful degrade' vs 'prioritized throughput' modes.
3) Produce an auditable billing model that shows per-burst attribution and proration rules; update billing pipelines and invoice templates.
4) Provide telemetry so SRE/CS/Customers can reason about burst cost, latency, and hit-rate.

Proposed design (high level):
- Admission policy: requests tagged with burst_token are accepted into surge pool only if (a) fleet surge headroom exists, (b) customer burst_quota > 0, and (c) runtime prechecks pass (model variant available, memory headroom). Admission returns reason codes (ADMITTED / QUEUED / REJECTED).
- Warm-up window: admitted bursts go through a short warm-up (configurable 10-60s) to prime KV caches; metrics emitted for warm-up token counts and cold-first-token latency.
- Sustain & eviction: each customer has two modes: GUARANTEED_BURST (dedicated units reserved from surge pool for a short window, billed at reserved rate) or BEST_EFFORT_BURST (use surge only if unused; billed at overage rate). Eviction policy uses LRU per-customer scoring and a fairness factor to avoid starvation.
- Spend caps & soft-fallbacks: Console/API exposes burst_spend_cap and burst_mode. When cap reached, we either (a) switch to degraded model variant (lower throughput) or (b) return 429 with explicit billing hint.
- Billing attribution: burst usage is recorded as granular events (timestamp, tokens_generated, admission_reason, billing_tier). Billing jobs will aggregate per-burst events and apply proration for partial-minute reservations. Invoice line items include a unique burst_id and a human-readable explanation bucket.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Runtime implements admission/warm-up/sustain/evict lifecycle with logs and reason codes.
- Console shows per-fleet and per-customer burst spend and the active burst_mode toggle.
- Billing pipeline emits per-burst events and test invoices correctly show attributed burst charges with burst_id.
- E2E test that simulates burst and validates billing and graceful degrade behavior.
- Documentation and customer-facing KB article that explains the two burst modes and how to set caps.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Complexity vs predictability: implementing GUARANTEED_BURST requires reserving surge headroom (reduces pool for others). We must decide default mode (suggest: BEST_EFFORT by default).
- Warm-up latency: strict warm-up improves QoE but increases cost; need to tune defaults per model family.
- Billing granularity: per-token events increase pipeline volume; consider sampling or batching strategies for high-throughput customers.

Implementation notes / areas of work:
- runtime/allocator: admission logic, scoring function, reason-code schema (ENG team).
- billing: new event schema, aggregation, invoice template updates (Billing team).
- console/api: burst_mode toggle, spend cap input, and burst spend UI (Console team).
- docs/comms: KB article, FAQ, and update to SLA docs (Docs & CS).

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: customers accidentally incur high overage charges. Mitigation: default spend_cap = small value for new accounts, and add explicit opt-in for GUARANTEED_BURST.
- Risk: telemetry blowup. Mitigation: limit burst-event retention to 90d and sample high-frequency customers for raw token-level events.

Notes on related tickets: this ticket depends on low-level surge metrics (ENG-7421) and earlier transient quota work (ENG-8532).
